Limit is a competitive strategy game where you play as a Nation facing the challenges of our world. Make crucial political decisions, manage your resources with finesse, anticipate global crises and adapt to the upheavals of the planet and the decisions of other Nations. Balance growth and resilience to build a prosperous society.

The game takes place in a maximum of 7 generations. However, the end of the game can come before if you and your opponents trigger at least 4 global crises.

A generation is made up of 3 phases:


     The Political phase: you make decisions
     The Social phase: your Nation reacts to these decisions
     The International phase: crises arise and alliances are formed


End of the Game:
Before counting your points, you must test the resilience of your Nation for future generations. Redo the Food, Consumption and Production stages of the Social phase with the effects of shortages but without new crises.

The Nation with the highest score wins the game.

Does it reward only growing in the end phase? Yes. Is there something that is or feels positive while playing? No! Mostly playing by himself? Yes. Convoluted rules for every phase? Absolutely! Inspiring? No. Boring? Absolutely!

[Rating: 2/10] Great architecture of thematic ideas brought to design ruined by abandoning the idea of play for the political pamphletism of scoring.  I wouldn't play it again.

[Rating: 2/10] Takes all the fun parts of Hegemony (asymmetry, faction fighting on the margin, interaction) and gets rid of them to deliver yet another resource trading lever puller where you don't need to look up from your board until the end.  [EDIT] - After another bit of play, yeah, there's nothing to this one. Wouldn't play it again.

[Rating: 3/10] Don't bother maximizing your houses and population. Maybe they would have sold it better as cooperative game where you need not to trigger 4 catastrophes and survive 7 generations.

[Rating: 3/10] It was supposed to be an amazing experience/experiment. Unfortunately the experience is underwhelming and the game is straight up mediocre with the final prescore round and scoring simply bad.

[Rating: 3/10] It's just not fun:) Once the oil runs out that's it - winner is the one that crashes the least?  Or do you avoid growing your industry to need oil - but then your population revolts because they're not getting the goods they need.  I found it extremely frustrating and couldn't wait for it to end.

[Rating: 3/10] This game is backed up by an interesting theory, but have underwhelming gameplay in a few prospects.  First, managing your country in this game is playing 1-2 cards, then watching it push itself on several tracks. Way too abtract and repeatitive.  Second, this game simply feeds you the Limit hypothesis and you have to swallow. You don't get to test the theory and explore where your limits are. You have no say in this. In fact, you are just a tireless robot pushing the tracks.

[Rating: 3/10] Play cards to move some tracks up and some tracks down. Rinse and repeat endlessly. Moving two steps forward and one step back is more fun.
